goal: Refactor the SDD flow definition/registry boundary so registry.js remains the CLI command registry while definition-side APIs own lifecycle decisions derived from the flow structure.

in: must: Keep registry.js as the CLI command registry while removing direct lifecycle decisions from hooks.
must: Add definition-side APIs for node lookup, task node lookup, maxAttempts, sideEffects, runtime step resolution, lifecycle resolution, active node lookup, and definition order queries.
must: Represent lifecycle actions as dedicated classes with constructor-enforced invariants instead of object literal action records.
must: Move flow.json steps-array-only utilities to a dedicated step-tree module.
must: Remove raw FLOW_DEFINITION/TASK_DEFINITION exports and update production modules, helper modules, and tests to use APIs or step-tree utilities.
must: Preserve existing flow CLI command names, options, help text, JSON envelope shapes, step ids, status transitions, and exit behavior.
out: must: Avoid external dependencies and TypeScript migration.
must: Avoid backward-compatible aliases for raw definition exports.
must: Keep complex finalize git, filesystem, metadata, report, and issue-comment side effects in normal handler modules behind lifecycle hook actions.

constraints: Only Node.js built-in modules may be used; no external dependency may be added.
The alpha policy applies: old raw definition exports must be removed instead of preserved as compatibility aliases.
Meaningful lifecycle values must be represented by dedicated classes that enforce invariants in constructors.
No user-facing flow command, option, help text, JSON envelope shape, step id, status transition, or exit-code contract may change unless the spec is reopened and explicitly approved.
No new CLI command or user-facing argument is introduced by this spec; validate-user-input-at-entry-point and exit-code-contract guardrails are satisfied by preserving existing command entry points.
Docs are source-generated. Rebuild/update docs only if implementation changes documented flow internals.
design_principles: Keep registry.js deep enough for command metadata and dispatch wiring, but make lifecycle decisions query definition-side APIs.
Separate data-structure traversal from flow definition knowledge: steps-array utilities belong in a step-tree module, while definition order and lifecycle resolution stay definition-side.
Use declarative lifecycle action classes for simple status, skip, metric, issue-log, and side-effect decisions; use hook actions as escape hatches for complex execution side effects.
Make the new boundary visible in tests so raw definition data does not remain an implicit contract.

modules.text: src/flow/definition.js defines flow and task nodes, definition-side query APIs, lifecycle action classes, and lifecycle resolution.
src/flow/lib/step-tree.js will own utilities that operate only on flow.json steps arrays, such as flattenSteps, findStepById, findFirstPendingLeaf, and findInProgressLeaf.
src/flow/registry.js remains the flow command registry and delegates lifecycle post/onError decisions through definition-side APIs or shared lifecycle application helpers.

src/flow/lib/gate-step.js, get-next-action.js, run-gate.js, run-review.js, get-status.js, flow-store.js, flow-manager.js, flow-helpers.js, skill-rules.js, and tests are expected consumers of the new APIs or step-tree utilities.

data_flow.text: A flow command runs through registry.js, which supplies command metadata and invokes command modules.
Registry hook connection points call lifecycle application helpers instead of hardcoding phase maps, step ids, or status transitions.
Definition-side APIs resolve nodes, maxAttempts, sideEffects, runtime log steps, lifecycle actions, and definition order from encapsulated flow/task definitions.
Step-tree utilities read and mutate flow.json step arrays without importing raw definition data.

decisions.evidence: src/flow/definition.js exports FLOW_DEFINITION/TASK_DEFINITION, resolveNodeFor, deriveNextAction, findActiveNode, flattenSteps, findStepById, findFirstPendingLeaf, and findInProgressLeaf.

decisions.text: [VERIFY] Checked draft policy: registry.js currently contains lifecycle decisions; result=match.

decisions.text: Treat every lifecycle leak named in Issue #370 as in scope when the decision is derivable from the definition.
decisions.evidence: Draft QA q1 answered that review status transitions, gate step resolution, finalize downstream skip/reset behavior, sideEffects, maxAttempts, and runtime log step resolution are acceptance criteria.

decisions.text: Use dedicated lifecycle action classes and remove object literal action records from lifecycle definitions.
decisions.evidence: Draft QA q2 and project rules require OOP-based value representation with constructor-enforced invariants.

decisions.text: Preserve user-visible CLI behavior while changing internal ownership.
decisions.evidence: Draft QA q3 and Issue #370 keep registry.js as the CLI command registry for commands, args, help, requirements, and hook connection points.

decisions.text: Remove raw definition data as an import contract for production, helpers, and tests.
decisions.evidence: Draft QA q4 and rg evidence show FLOW_DEFINITION/TASK_DEFINITION imports in src/lib/flow-helpers.js, src/lib/skill-rules.js, src/flow/lib/*, and tests.

decisions.text: [VERIFY] Checked review findings: draft PASS lifecycle includes required empty draft triage/repair artifact generation, and impl review proposals include evidence reset plus downstream step reset.

background: The SDD flow currently has a blurred boundary between definition.js and registry.js. definition.js is the flow blueprint, but it also exposes raw definition data and owns generic steps-array utilities. registry.js is the CLI command registry, but it contains flow lifecycle decisions such as runtime step maps, review status transitions, gate step resolution through registry-side maps, and finalize downstream skip/reset behavior. Issue #370 requests a responsibility cleanup: registry.js remains the command registry, while decisions derivable from the flow definition move to definition-side APIs.

requirements.desc: definition.js shall stop exporting raw FLOW_DEFINITION and TASK_DEFINITION and instead expose definition-side APIs for node lookup, task node lookup, leaf id collection, phase/action mapping, definition order, active node lookup, maxAttempts, sideEffects, runtime step resolution, and lifecycle resolution.
Steps-array-only utilities shall move out of definition.js into a dedicated step-tree module, and all consumers shall import those utilities from the step-tree module.

FlowNode or equivalent definition-side node objects shall carry lifecycle behavior using dedicated action classes with constructor-enforced invariants for status transitions, keep-in-progress behavior, metric increments, issue-log appends, side-effect execution, skip behavior, and hook escape hatches.

Definition-side lifecycle resolution shall cover review/gate/finalize status transitions, draft PASS empty triage/repair artifact generation, implementation-review proposal evidence reset from test-execute through finalize-cleanup, downstream skip/reset behavior, sideEffects, maxAttempts, and runtime log step resolution for the lifecycle cases named in Issue #370.

registry.js hooks shall delegate lifecycle decisions to definition-side APIs or shared lifecycle application helpers and shall not hardcode flow step ids, review phase maps, gate phase maps, or finalize downstream leaf lists for definition-derived decisions.
Production modules, helper modules, and tests shall be migrated away from raw definition imports so no caller depends on FLOW_DEFINITION or TASK_DEFINITION as exported data.
Existing flow CLI command names, options, help text, JSON envelope shapes, step ids, status transitions, and exit behavior shall remain user-visible compatible after the refactor.

Spec-local tests shall verify the new definition/registry boundary, raw export removal, step-tree utility relocation, lifecycle action class invariants, draft PASS artifact preservation, implementation-review proposal evidence reset, and representative review/gate/finalize lifecycle transitions.
If implementation changes documented flow internals, docs shall be rebuilt or updated through the project flow; otherwise docs shall remain unchanged.

acceptance_criteria: A reviewer can inspect src/flow/definition.js and confirm raw FLOW_DEFINITION/TASK_DEFINITION exports are absent while definition-side APIs provide the required query and lifecycle operations.
A reviewer can inspect src/flow/lib/step-tree.js and confirm steps-array utilities live there, with production and test imports updated to that module.
A reviewer can inspect lifecycle definitions and confirm lifecycle action values are dedicated classes rather than object literal action records.

A reviewer can inspect src/flow/registry.js and confirm hook entries delegate lifecycle decisions instead of hardcoding review phase maps, gate step ids, or finalize downstream leaf lists for definition-derived behavior.
A reviewer can inspect lifecycle handling and confirm draft review PASS still writes or invokes the existing empty draft triage/repair artifact generation before draft-gate validation.
A reviewer can inspect lifecycle handling and confirm proposal-producing implementation reviews still reset rebuildable evidence and downstream leaves from test-execute through finalize-cleanup.
Spec-local tests under specs/283-flow-definition-lifecycle/tests/ cover R1 through R8 using // spec: R<N> headers.
Existing shared unit/e2e tests that rely on flow behavior continue to pass, and full regression remains deferred to final-regression.
No user-facing flow command, option, help text, JSON envelope shape, step id, status transition, or exit behavior is changed by the diff.

clarifications.a: No. registry.js remains the CLI command registry and keeps command metadata plus hook connection points.

clarifications.q: Does this spec introduce a new CLI command, option, argument, or exit-code contract?
clarifications.a: No. CLI entry points are preserved; user-facing input validation and exit behavior remain unchanged.

clarifications.q: Do complex finalize git/filesystem/report side effects become declarative lifecycle primitives?
clarifications.a: No. They stay in normal handler modules and are reached through lifecycle hook escape hatches.

clarifications.q: Can old raw definition exports remain as compatibility aliases?
clarifications.a: No. The alpha policy and Issue #370 require removing raw exports rather than preserving aliases.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep raw FLOW_DEFINITION/TASK_DEFINITION exports during a phased migration.
alternatives_considered.reason: Rejected because alpha policy prohibits backward-compatible migration aliases and raw exports would keep the old structure as an active contract.

alternatives_considered.option: Move only one registry lifecycle leak in this spec.
alternatives_considered.reason: Rejected because Issue #370 names the registry/definition boundary as one concern and project rules prohibit splitting the user-defined Issue by default.

alternatives_considered.option: Represent lifecycle actions as object literals with type fields.
alternatives_considered.reason: Rejected because project rules require OOP-based value representation for meaningful values.

alternatives_considered.option: Push all finalize behavior into declarative lifecycle configuration.
alternatives_considered.reason: Rejected because Issue #370 explicitly keeps complex git/filesystem/report behavior in normal JavaScript functions behind an escape hatch.

tasks.title: Extract step-tree utilities
tasks.goal: Move steps-array-only utilities out of definition.js into a dedicated step-tree module.
acceptance: The new step-tree module exports flattenSteps, findStepById, findFirstPendingLeaf, findInProgressLeaf, and related steps-array-only helpers.
definition.js no longer owns helpers that operate only on flow.json steps arrays.
Current production and test imports for steps-array-only helpers point to the step-tree module.
tasks.implementation_notes: Keep utilities bounded in the same way existing traversal helpers are bounded. Do not move definition-order helpers that require flow/task definition knowledge.
tasks.test_strategy: Spec-local static tests assert the step-tree module exports the utilities and definition.js no longer exports those steps-array-only helpers.

tasks.title: Encapsulate definition access
tasks.goal: Replace raw definition data exports with definition-side query APIs for flow and task definition access.
acceptance: FLOW_DEFINITION and TASK_DEFINITION are not exported as raw data.
Definition-side APIs provide node lookup, task node lookup, leaf id collection, phase/action mapping, definition order, active node lookup, maxAttempts, sideEffects, and runtime step resolution.
Callers no longer pass raw definition data into generic resolver functions.
tasks.implementation_notes: Use deep module design: callers ask intent-specific APIs instead of knowing the definition data shape.
tasks.test_strategy: Spec-local static tests assert raw exports are absent and representative modules import/call definition APIs instead.

tasks.title: Model lifecycle actions
tasks.goal: Add lifecycle action classes and attach declarative lifecycle behavior to flow definition nodes where simple lifecycle decisions are definition-derived.
acceptance: Lifecycle actions are class instances with constructor validation.
Lifecycle definitions cover status transitions, keep-in-progress behavior, metric increments, issue-log appends, side-effect execution, skip behavior, and hook escape hatches.
Complex finalize execution behavior is represented by hook actions that call existing handler modules rather than declarative primitives.
tasks.implementation_notes: Keep primitive vocabulary small and use normal JavaScript handlers for git/filesystem/report side effects.
tasks.test_strategy: Spec-local unit tests instantiate lifecycle classes and assert invalid constructor inputs throw.

tasks.title: Delegate registry lifecycle
tasks.goal: Update registry.js hooks so lifecycle decisions are applied through definition-side lifecycle resolution instead of registry-local hardcoded maps and step ids.
acceptance: Review runtime step resolution is delegated to definition-side lifecycle or runtime-step APIs.
Draft review PASS lifecycle writes or invokes existing empty draft triage/repair artifact generation before draft-gate validation.
Proposal-producing implementation review lifecycle resets rebuildable evidence and downstream leaves from test-execute through finalize-cleanup while keeping impl-review open.
Gate step resolution used by registry hooks is delegated to definition-side APIs.
Finalize downstream skip/reset decisions are derived from definition-side lifecycle rules.
Registry command entries still contain command metadata, args, help, requirements, and hook connection points.
tasks.implementation_notes: Preserve registry.js as the command registry. Shared lifecycle application helpers may live outside registry.js if that keeps registry entries thin.
tasks.test_strategy: Spec-local tests assert registry.js no longer contains the old phase maps/downstream leaf lists, draft PASS artifact generation is preserved, implementation-review proposal evidence reset is preserved, and representative lifecycle transitions still update steps as expected.

tasks.title: Migrate definition consumers
tasks.goal: Update production modules, helper modules, and tests to use the new definition APIs and step-tree module while preserving flow behavior.
acceptance: No source or test import depends on raw FLOW_DEFINITION/TASK_DEFINITION exports.
Existing flow helper, gate, review, status, next-action, flow-store, flow-manager, and skill-rules behavior remains covered by tests.
Existing shared regression tests are updated only to match the new module boundary, not weakened.
tasks.implementation_notes: Use rg to find all old imports and update them consistently. Keep unrelated refactors out of scope.
tasks.test_strategy: Spec-local static tests plus existing unit/e2e tests cover import migration and behavioral compatibility.
